lessons: Drive storm escalations from the journaled `storm_trip` signal itself, not from its lazily created `control_hold`. Holds exist only after dispatch offers the origin, so startup reconcile misses trips. This overrides the earlier lesson that said to drive storm notices from the control_hold.
Key storm notifications as effect_key('notify', emitting_origin, 'storm_trip', trip_id), so the key stays the same whether or not a hold exists later. Keep red-streak keys on hold_id unchanged.

Resume action: if an unreleased storm_trip control_hold matches trip_id, render `squatch resume --hold-id <hold_id>`. If not, read daemon.py StormDispatchHold and the resume verb, then render the real pull-side action for a pending trip. Never render a placeholder.
Add a test_notify startup case that journals only a storm_trip signal with no hold and asserts it is sent. Add a test_serve case asserting it is sent before the first dispatch.

In SubprocessNotifications.notify, turn launch OSErrors other than FileNotFoundError (e.g. PermissionError, IsADirectoryError) into RuntimeError. Add a test_seams case with a non-executable file as argv[0], plus a reconciler test that it is reported and no completion is journaled.

Keep what passed review: seam isolation, config validator, red-streak keys, _serve wiring, startup-then-poll ordering, unset warning, replay suppression, timeout handling. Change only notify.py, seams.py and their tests, and add the serve startup case.
Re-run all three Verification commands before committing. The soak suites must stay unchanged and green.
reason: Review found two concrete, fixable defects: storm trips without a hold are missed at startup, and non-FileNotFound OSErrors can crash serve. Both have clear fixes, so a retry at the same capability is enough.
